body:
# Protocol versioning — design of record

Decided with the maintainer on 2026-09-20. Until now the client/server interface had no version:
an installed app could silently misread data after a server upgrade. From 3.0.0 on the interface
has an integer **protocol version**, and a client that is too old for the server is turned away
and sent to the update mechanism instead of misbehaving.

## Policy

* `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is a single integer. It is **3** from release 3.0.0 on. (Clients before
  3.0.0 send nothing; the server treats that as "older than any version".)
* A change to the client/server interface that an already-installed client of the previous
  protocol cannot handle correctly bumps PROTOCOL_VERSION, and the release that ships it is a new
  **MAJOR** version. Additive changes an old client simply ignores (a new optional response field,
  a new endpoint the old client never calls) do not bump it. The protocol version never exceeds the
  release's major version (a major release without a protocol change, like a rebrand, leaves it
  alone).
* The server is upgraded before its clients. A client whose protocol is HIGHER than the server's
  is not refused by the server (an older server cannot know); it is the operator's job not to run
  a newer app against an older server.
* `docs/wire-contract.md` gets a "Protocol version" section: the rule above and a changelog table
  (protocol 3, introduced in 3.0.0: ledger entry types). Every future bump adds a row saying what
  broke.

## The wire

* Every request to the API carries the header `X-Client-Protocol: <integer>`.
* The server (the blueprint, applied before authentication, to every API route of the instance
  except `GET /app-version`) compares it with PROTOCOL_VERSION. If the header is missing, not a
  plain positive integer, or lower than PROTOCOL_VERSION, the answer is
  `426 {"error": "client_outdated", "message": "...", "protocol": <server's PROTOCOL_VERSION>}`
  and nothing else happens (no auth, no database access, no audit record, no housekeeping).
  Equal or higher passes.
* `GET /app-version` stays reachable by an outdated client (it is how the app finds the update)
  and gains a field `"protocol": <PROTOCOL_VERSION>` next to `version` and `download_url`.
* Site-root routes (`/`, `/invite/<token>`, the web bundle, `/shoppinglist.apk`) are not gated.
* New error code `client_outdated` (426) in the wire-contract error table, in
  `web/src/i18n/apiErrors.ts` and `android/.../ui/ErrorText.kt`, in all nine locales, paired by
  identical English across the two clients.
* Constants: `server/src/shoppinglist_server/protocol.py` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 3`,
  `PROTOCOL_HEADER = "X-Client-Protocol"`), `web/src/api/protocol.ts`, and a `Protocol.kt` in
  the Android data/api package. A web test reads all three and asserts they are equal (the way
  crossClient.test.ts reads the Android resources).

## Release guard

`release.sh` refuses (before writing anything, with the other preconditions) when:
* the working tree's PROTOCOL_VERSION is greater than the new release's MAJOR; or
* PROTOCOL_VERSION is greater than it was at the previous release tag, unless the new release's
  MAJOR is greater than the previous tag's MAJOR.
A previous tag without `protocol.py` counts as protocol 0. The logic lives in a small script that
unit tests can call (with the four numbers as arguments), not only inline in release.sh; server
tests cover it, including the refusals.

## What a client does on 426 / client_outdated

* **Web.** The bundle is served by the same server, so a reload fetches the current one. Show
  nothing intermediate: reload the page once automatically (remember the attempt in
  sessionStorage with a timestamp so it cannot loop). If a 426 arrives again within five minutes
  of that reload, show a full-page notice instead (title "Update required", body "The server has
  been updated. Reload this page to continue.", a Reload button) and stop syncing.
* **Android.** A request answered 426 must (a) not count as a session end (no forced logout),
  (b) not count as a row error (nothing is quarantined, no dirty row is dropped or blocked, no
  local data is wiped), and (c) stop the sync/worker from hammering the server until the app has
  been updated. It raises an app-wide "update required" state, and the root of the UI shows a
  blocking full-screen notice that AUTOMATICALLY starts the existing update mechanism (the
  UpdateChecker check, ignoring the auto-check switch and the rate limit, because this one is not
  optional) and then offers the download/install exactly as the existing update prompt does. If
  the server has no app to offer (404 no_app_package) or the check fails, the notice says the app
  is too old for this server and that its operator has to provide an update, with a Retry action.
  After a successful install the app restarts, which clears the state; if the state is somehow
  cleared without an update, the next 426 raises it again.
* Both clients send the header on EVERY API request, including login and register.

## Old apps in the field (documented, not solved)

An installed 2.x app sends no header and does not know the code, so after the server upgrade it
gets 426 and shows its generic failure message; its existing foreground update check (twice a day)
and the About screen's check will offer the new version. The 3.0.0 release notes (written at
release time, not now) must say that every device has to be updated together with the server.
title: Protocol versioning: a too-old client is turned away and sent to the update mechanism (design)
